front.title: Cognitive Reconciliation for YANG and TM Forum Model Interoperability

abstract.t: Network operators must make YANG-modeled service and network interfaces interoperate with TM Forum (TMF) OSS/BSS APIs. Today this is done with hand-built, model-specific adapters, whose construction and maintenance is ongoing human work. The ONSEN problem statement records the absence of a standard alignment between TMF APIs and YANG models as an open problem. This document applies ad hoc semantic reconciliation by cognitive agents, as developed in draft-janz-nmrg- adhoc-semantic-reconciliation, to that problem. Two cognitive agents lift their respective models, bind through a thin shared reference, and each generates and operates its own inbound translator, with no model-specific adapter agreed in advance. This document reports results from a demonstrator whose first case reconciles the L3SM service model to a TMF representation. It runs the reconciliation in two forms, one anchored on the mapping-root annotations of draft-lls- onsen-yang-tmf-mapping, and one with those annotations withheld, in which the agents must locate the services themselves in the plain model, and the two forms together size what the annotations contribute. It shows the reconciled mapping operating on real instance data, shows the model-drift lifecycle by which the translators are kept current, reads the demonstrator as an empirical point on a cognition-placement spectrum, from over-arching cognition over two inert systems to both systems cognitive, and is explicit about what over-arching cognition achieves when neither system is itself cognitive. A second case reconciles the L3SM service model to the L3NM network model, a cross-abstraction mapping where a cognitive counterpart earns its place, so the two cases together give the two poles of the spectrum on two ONSEN problem areas. The document closes with recommendations for operational practice and for standardization.
